reason: Experiment 4, with_ai, ai_vs_active. Both candidates are full-sample analyses of the same ChatGPT-versus-Web arms. Tie rule: among analyses of the same contrast, the one whose statistics allow a participant-level standardized effect. The pooled comparison (Supplementary Information) prints arm means, participant-level SDs, and t(396) = 3.29; the ANOVA main effect prints only F(1,396) = 5.06 and partial eta squared. Both proposers left the tie open because they read the rule as also requiring arm counts.

Experiment 5, with_ai, ai_vs_active: same reasoning as Experiment 4 (pooled comparison with arm means, participant-level SDs, and t(379) = 8.67, against an ANOVA main effect with F and partial eta squared only).

Lee and Chung Experiment 4 (shared sample), across_people: Lee and Chung report no diversity outcome, so this reanalysis supplies it (rule 4). The paper prints diversity only within the cells of the 2 x 2 design. Tie rule: the cell at the crossed factor's least modified level. Low constraints means two constraints, against six in the high condition (Lee and Chung, Experiment 4 arms).
Lee and Chung Experiment 5 (shared sample), across_people: as for Experiment 4. The base cell uses the baseline scenario; the high-empathy cell adds that the items were adored by one's daughter.

across_people, ai_vs_bau: SBERT similarity is the paper's similarity measure (rule 2 for across_people); among repeated sessions, Day 2 is the first session with ChatGPT (tie rule for repeated sessions; the paper prints no pooled estimate and its abstract names no day). The two tasks remain tied; Task 2 is chosen so that both primary records of this sample come from one task (the with_ai primary, agreed by both proposers, is Task 2 novelty on Day 2).

with_ai, ai_vs_active. Four AI arms share the human-example control and differ in AI dose (two or four of six examples from ChatGPT) and in labeling. Rule 3: High Exposure, Disclosed is closest to free use of a chatbot, where every suggestion comes from the AI and the user knows it. The paper reports no contrast of all AI arms combined.

across_people, ai_vs_active. Median pairwise cosine distance is the paper's main diversity metric (mean pairwise and centroid distances are its robustness variants); the global level of diversity answers the across-people question, while the slope records describe how diversity evolves along the chains. Arm: High Exposure, Disclosed, as for the with_ai record (rule 3).

across_people, ai_design. Main metric (median pairwise distance). Among the six AI-versus-AI contrasts, the dose contrast (four versus two AI examples) with labeling held at the disclosed level, the level of chatbot use; the disclosure contrasts stay on the study page.

with_ai, ai_vs_bau, shared sample with Balta-Salvador et al. (2025). First round only (Review 1 Decision 11). Both remaining candidates are novelty counts; Originality (unique ideas plus unique solutions) is the paper's originality index, while the Existing Solutions count tallies non-novel solutions and rises with the number of ideas.

with_ai, ai_design. Among regression specifications of the same contrast, the one with no added covariates (tie rule added 2026-10-11, for review): the plain randomized contrast, closest to a difference in arm means; the other columns add fixed effects or controls.

with_ai, ai_vs_bau. Rule 3: GPT Only is closest to free chatbot use (GPT + Overview adds prompt-engineering training). Among regression specifications of the same contrast, the one with no added covariates (tie rule added 2026-10-11, for review): the plain randomized contrast, closest to a difference in arm means; the other columns add fixed effects or controls. Column (1) also gives the 17.9 percent increase the paper reports.

with_ai, ai_design. Among regression specifications of the same contrast, the one with no added covariates (tie rule added 2026-10-11, for review): the plain randomized contrast, closest to a difference in arm means; the other columns add fixed effects or controls.

with_ai, ai_vs_bau. A 2 x 2 design (AI by teaming): the contrast at the crossed factor's baseline level (individuals), in which AI access is the only difference; Team + AI versus Individual No AI also changes teaming. Among regression specifications of the same contrast, the one with no added covariates (tie rule added 2026-10-11, for review): the plain randomized contrast, closest to a difference in arm means; the other columns add fixed effects or controls.
across_people, ai_vs_bau. As for the with_ai record: the contrast at the baseline level of teaming, in which AI access is the only difference between the arms.

after_ai, ai_vs_bau. The acquisition test repeats the item used during AI instruction ('books'), so its originality can reflect recall of ideas from the AI dialogue; the transfer items are new to the participant and measure the person's own skill, the after_ai question (tie rule added 2026-10-11, for review).
after_ai, ai_vs_active. As for the comparison with the rest control: the transfer items, new to the participant.

with_ai, ai_vs_bau. Both candidates are randomized within an initial group (the initial A/B allocation is not described as random). B1 versus B2 compares AI access with no AI among people who had not used AI before, as in single-session studies; A1 versus A2 compares keeping with withdrawing AI after an AI-assisted first draft.

across_people, ai_vs_active. Two tests of the same contrast and score; neither allows a standardized effect. The Mann-Whitney test asks whether one arm's stories are more or less diverse, the across-people question; the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test detects any difference in the shape of the distribution.

with_ai, ai_vs_active. Originality first (outcome order). Two active comparators share the ChatGPT arm: Google search and a human peer. Web search is the active comparator that the other ai_vs_active studies use most, so the pooled contrast stays comparable; the human-peer contrast stays on the study page.

across_people, ai_vs_bau. Neither group-level count is a semantic-similarity measure. The count of distinct conceptual domains across each arm's pool measures how varied the ideas are across people; the count of different uses tracks the number of ideas. Same choice as the paper's with_ai record (flexibility over fluency).
across_people, ai_vs_bau. Category coverage compares the two arms' pooled ideas; the light-ring share is printed for the AI arm only, with no control value, so it cannot show a comparison.

with_ai, ai_design. FREE-FORM is free use of default ChatGPT (rule 3 reference arm). STRUCTURED is the approach the abstract describes as 'informed by a theory of reframing', so this contrast asks whether a designed interaction beats free use; the other two contrasts stay on the study page.

with_ai, ai_design (proposers disagreed). The paper names its main specification: 'we included only problem-solving skill and creativity as control variables in our main analyses' (Method, Control variables). Rule: the paper's main specification first; the no-added-covariates fallback applies only when the paper does not single one out.

after_ai, ai_vs_active (proposers disagreed). Two scripted AI teammates share the human-only control. Rule 3: the supportive persona, which invites input and builds on suggestions, is closer to ordinary chatbot use than the contrarian persona, which is instructed to challenge and dismiss suggestions.

across_people, ai_vs_bau (proposers disagreed). Metric: 'All plots use the embedding model all-MiniLM-L12-v2. See Appendix C.2 for other metrics as robustness checks' (Section 5.2). Cell of the 2 x 2 (AI by incentive): neither incentive is a no-incentive level, and the main-text results compare AI-O with 'the SELF baseline' under the originality incentive, so AI-O versus SELF-O.

with_ai, ai_vs_bau (proposers disagreed). Main specification: the strata-adjusted intention-to-treat model (Section 3.3, Table 2). Rule 3: Full treatment gives chatbot access from problem formulation onward and is closest to free use; the introduction's mention of the Partial arm reports a result and does not name a primary contrast.

across_people, ai_vs_bau. Both candidates compare the Full arm with arms unassisted during problem formulation; the Control arm never had AI, while the Partial arm had AI later in the task, so Full versus Control is the plain comparison (same arm as the with_ai primary).

with_ai, ai_design, shared sample with Chen et al. (2026). The two papers report the same paired originality contrast with the same means (2.92 and 3.13) and p = 0.098; this record also prints the number of people analyzed (62), which a standard error needs, while the 2026 record gives a z statistic without it.

across_people, ai_design. Human Confirmation is the paper's reference arm in its regressions, and Copilot is the arm closest to free chatbot use; the same pair is this sample's agreed with_ai ai_design primary.

across_people, ai_vs_bau. The across_people rule names the paper's semantic-similarity measure; cosine similarity is that measure, and the L2 distance is an alternative distance on the same embeddings.

with_ai, ai_design. All four candidates are the paper's planned Welch contrasts. C3 (AI throughout the process) is the arm closest to free chatbot use; against C1 (AI during divergent search only) it isolates when AI is available, while the C5 contrasts add a warning, a second manipulation.

with_ai, ai_vs_active. Text and image quality are parallel primary outcomes. The ad copy is what the participant writes with the partner; images come from Dall-E 3 in both arms, so the text rating reflects the collaboration the arms differ in.
with_ai, ai_design. Three levels of researcher control within one agentic system; the contrast of the highest with the lowest level spans the design factor.

across_people, ai_vs_bau. Rule 3: unconstrained GenAI access is closest to free chatbot use (as for the agreed with_ai primary). Cosine similarity is the semantic-similarity measure; the dispersion index is its complement (1 - CosSim).
across_people, ai_design. Cosine similarity, as for the ai_vs_bau record; the dispersion index is its complement.

with_ai, ai_vs_bau. Two summaries of the same novelty contrast: the t-test record prints arm means and participant-level SDs (Table 2), the inputs of a standardized effect; the condition correlation is another summary of the same data.

with_ai, ai_vs_active. The with_ai question concerns what the person produces, so the human participant's own ideas, not the whole-dyad outputs that include ideas the AI wrote. Tasks: AUT, the divergent-thinking task most studies in this pool use; PIT stays on the study page.

with_ai, ai_vs_bau. Three LLM judges rate the same stories. FIERO generates text with GPT-4, and the paper cites evidence that LLM judges favor LLM-written text (its reference 53), so the GPT-5.2 judge is set aside; Claude Opus 4.5 is the first of the two remaining judges in the paper's order. No record has a standard error, so none is pooled.

with_ai, ai_design. Final creativity (the paper's main analysis, as both proposers found). The timing contrast with labeling held at the labeled level: this sample's with_ai primary uses the labeled arm, and labeled AI ideas are closer to chatbot use, where the user knows the source (as for Ashkinaze et al.). The proposers' unlabeled pair is superseded.

after_ai, ai_vs_active. The AI teammates are undisclosed, so no arm resembles chatbot use. Two humans and one supportive AI is the least modified AI team (one teammate replaced), and the supportive persona is closer to ordinary assistant behavior than the contrarian one (as for Jin et al. 2026b).

after_ai, ai_vs_active (supplementary replication 1). Cosine similarity, the semantic-similarity measure. Rule 3: the standard ChatGPT (GPT-4o) arm is closer to free use of a general chatbot than the arm that adds live source links; the two proposers chose the same arm for this sample's word counts in batch 2.
